fact: The UN Economic Commission for Africa, with GIZ and the EU and the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy, ran consultations and workshops on 2-9 June 2026 to support development of a National Data Governance Strategy for digital sovereignty.

The AfDB president said the national TIER III+ data centre in Brazzaville, costing about EUR 66.55 million with EUR 14.50 million from the Congolese government, would open by May 2026 as a tool of digital sovereignty giving secure, independent storage of the country's data.

The minister of digital economy said the national data centre under construction in Brazzaville (over 90% built) is meant to host the government's critical data, because e-government needs data sovereignty, with inauguration planned before 28 November 2025.

The minister of digital economy said the national data centre in Brazzaville, over 80% built and financed by the AfDB at USD 13 million, will let Congo store, process and host all its digital data and locally built applications, to guarantee its digital sovereignty.

The African Development Bank and Congo's backbone project coordinator describe a national data centre under construction in Brazzaville, about 60% of civil works done in May 2024, to host all public data and the national digital ID data in the country rather than abroad.
